study type: Longitudinal analysis of two prospective cohorts
exposure: Birth mode (Cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
cohort: The study analyzed data from 1402 children aged 2 to 36 months in the ELEMENT cohort and 726 children aged 5 to 27 months in the PROGRESS cohort, excluding those with maternal diseases like preeclampsia, renal or heart disease, gestational diabetes, and epilepsy.
finding: Children born by C-section showed lower motor and language development scores during specific age windows in the first three years of life.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with significantly lower psychomotor, motor, and language development scores at specific ages during early childhood compared to vaginal delivery.
